reasoning: The tweet presents a Keon Coleman and CeeDee Lamb training video as current offseason footage, but multiple sports outlets (SI, CBS Sports) confirm this is from May 2024 OTA sessions. Recycling old content as new is misleading.

The claim that TPUSA took 22% of NFL viewership is demonstrably false. TPUSA peaked at ~6.1 million concurrent viewers vs. Bad Bunny's 128.2 million on the Super Bowl broadcast. That's roughly 4-5%, not 22%. Multiple outlets (TV Insider, USA Today, CBS News) confirm these figures.

This is a personal statement by John Rocker about traveling to Colombia for stem cell treatment. There is no misleading factual claim — it's a first-person account of his own medical decision. The overwhelming consensus among existing notes is 'not misleading.'

The tweet frames the woman as a victim of unprovoked MAGA violence, but reporting from multiple outlets indicates she first physically confronted pro-ICE protesters and later fired a BB gun at them from her car. The bear spray was used in self-defense against her. The tweet omits critical context that changes the narrative significantly.

Two factual errors: (1) The show was not 'performed completely in Spanish' — Lady Gaga sang 'Die with a Smile' in English as a guest. (2) The implicit claim that Latino performers at the Super Bowl would have been unthinkable in 2000 is undercut by the fact that the Super Bowl XXXIV (2000) halftime featured Enrique Iglesias and Christina Aguilera, and was narrated by Edward James Olmos.

The tweet calls Ted Gunderson 'Former FBI director,' which is false. Gunderson was a Special Agent in Charge of several FBI field offices (Memphis, Dallas, Los Angeles) but was never FBI Director. He was interviewed for the position in 1979 but it went to William H. Webster.

The claim that 'over 6 MILLION have LEFT the Super Bowl channel' is misleading. While TPUSA peaked at ~6.1 million concurrent viewers, there is no evidence these viewers 'left' the Super Bowl broadcast, which had 128.2 million viewers. The Super Bowl audience was not meaningfully diminished.

The $800k lump sum claim appears fabricated or exaggerated. Other reports indicate Kai Cenat provided a $25k-$100k monthly allowance that was cut off, not an $800k one-time payment. The same account later posted a version claiming $50k instead, suggesting unreliable sourcing.

TMZ did post a poll on X asking which halftime show fans preferred, and Kid Rock won it with roughly 64-67%. While the tweet's framing is hyperbolic ('BRUTAL FLOP'), the core claim about a TMZ poll favoring Kid Rock is substantiated. The poll was real, though unscientific.

The core claim is largely accurate: Ye aired a Super Bowl ad (locally, not nationally) directing viewers to yeezy.com, which shortly after featured only a $20 swastika t-shirt labeled 'HH-01.' The $8M figure and 30-second duration are common descriptions. While it aired locally rather than nationally, the tweet's substance is confirmed by NBC News, Washington Post, and Variety.
